correctness.rationale: Exact uniform Dirichlet simplex one- and two-coordinate tails integrate to the stated covariance. After w=a/(1-a), logarithmic derivative of h=(1-w)^(n-1)(1+w)^n crosses sign once, proving exactly one interior zero (or n=2 boundary). The sparse scaling limit follows from controlled Taylor expansion; the positive limit root is unique. 5657 checker assertions independently confirm finite integral algebra and numerical limits, but the infinite claims use the written proof.

value.rationale: Gap count and total uncovered length are two operationally distinct failure measures for random circle coverage. The sharp finite-n reversal and nontrivial n a_n limit at the unique root of exp(c)=1+c+c^2 distinguish negative from positive dependence, informing when gap count is a misleading proxy for uncovered extent. This is more than recomputing either marginal distribution or reporting a single numerical instance.
